blocks.text: Networking devices are used to connect computers and other devices in a network. They control the flow of data, and each device has a specific role in communication.

blocks.caption: Networking devices and their jobs
rows: Lets a device connect to a network, wired or wireless. Each NIC has a unique address called the MAC address. It sends and receives the device's data; without a NIC a device cannot communicate on a network. NICs are built into most modern devices.
Connects devices within a network and sends data only to the correct device, which improves network speed and efficiency. Switches are common in modern networks.

Connects different networks together and directs data packets to their correct destination using IP addresses. Routers connect local networks to the Internet and improve security and control; home and office networks use them widely.

Connects a local network to an Internet Service Provider (ISP). It converts digital data into signals suitable for the line and converts incoming signals back into digital form. Modems are used with cable, DSL or fibre connections and often work with routers.
Provides Wi-Fi so that wireless devices can connect to a network. It extends wireless coverage and improves signal strength and stability in large buildings and campuses.

blocks.alt: A chain from left to right: a computer with a NIC card under it (joins a device to the network; has a unique MAC address), a switch (sends data to the correct device), a router (joins different networks; routes packets by IP), a modem (converts digital data to line signals and back) and a cloud labelled ISP and Internet. Below the router a wireless access point sends Wi-Fi to a laptop and a phone.
blocks.caption: Networking devices and their jobs (original diagram after Figs 1.6 and 1.7).
blocks.long_description: Data from a computer passes through its NIC to the switch, then to the router, which sends traffic for other networks through the modem to the ISP. The access point lets wireless devices join the same network.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: The teacher explains the modem with an example of signal conversion, and students summarise it.

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between a switch and a router?
blocks.explanation: A switch connects devices within one network and sends data to the correct device; a router connects different networks (for example a home network and the Internet) and directs packets between them using IP addresses.
The unique address of a network interface card (NIC), which identifies the device's network hardware.

items: NIC: joins a device to the network; MAC address.
Switch: devices within a network. Router: between networks, by IP.
Modem: digital data to line signals and back, to the ISP.
Access point: Wi-Fi for wireless devices.
